provenance.description: Advisory scheduling hypothesis from measured setup/call/teardown records; not acceptance evidence or proof of the 300-second target. Latest successful node observations replace earlier observations; failed or unexecuted nodes retain their previous observation. The first three shared-fixture groups retain consumer call/teardown costs plus one maximum observed cold setup charge assigned to the first sorted consumer. The fourth serial/resource-affinity group retains both independent nodes full setup/call/teardown costs without normalization. Its proposed serialization addresses possible nested-worker contention; speed benefit is unmeasured. Failed nodes remain timing observations, never reusable test evidence. The new ten-shard case has only a focused macOS observation. Its provisional platform weight conservatively takes the maximum of that observation and prior five/seven-shard node phase costs scaled to eleven fixture nodes. This scaling is an advisory assumption, not a measured hosted duration or acceptance proof.

group_sources.cost_policy: Full setup/call/teardown per node; no shared setup normalization.
group_sources.hypothesis: Serializing these two independent proofs may reduce overlapping nested-worker contention; no causal speedup is established.

provenance.collection_scope: Only the existing 2209 measured nodes per platform are included. No count-10 test node, duration, or provisional estimate is included.
prediction_limitations: Node durations vary with runner speed, co-location and worker concurrency.
The phase model excludes provisioning, worker startup, command overhead and cross-job launch skew.
No measured speedup is assumed for the fourth group; hosted execution and exact gates must establish acceptance.
The proposed ten-machine Windows partition has not been executed; its new public count-10 test still requires a separate real regression and measurement.

focused_source.state: Uncommitted count10 support; timing observation only

tests/test_verification_cache.py::test_r.limitation: Costs need not scale linearly; hosted phases must replace these provisional estimates.
